summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of Phase 73 (shared-write/navigation correctness for web) via wave-based parallel subagent orchestration, then follow up by fully consolidating a leftover dedup todo (`consolidate-web-shared-navigation-dup`) into the phase and closing it out.
summary.outcome: All 9 plans executed across 3 waves with clean merges and green gates; verifier found and the orchestrator fixed a real SC4 bug (missing publishedNode in refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey), re-verified 7/7; phase marked complete (final phase of v2.0 milestone). A follow-up agent then closed 3 of 4 remaining todo sub-items (readSharedContent dedup, ShareDialog export dedup, moot mirror) behind typecheck+eslint+35/35 live e2e verification, deliberately backed out of the risky 'resolveKinds-then-project' unification, and the todo was moved to completed with the back-out decision recorded as the resolution (final git mv/commit was in progress when the transcript ends).

repo: Cross-package types resolve via built dist/ (gitignored), so fresh worktrees need pnpm install + build of crypto→core→api-client→sdk-core→sdk chain before typecheck works

Root `pnpm typecheck` self-builds the full dependency chain and typechecks apps/web via tsc -b — this is what CI runs and is safe to use as the post-merge gate instead of full pnpm test (which includes flaky live-API integration tests)

gsd-executor agents are self-contained: they detect worktree mode via `.git` being a file, derive their own worktree identity, and emit a `<worktree_metadata>` JSON block; the harness (not the executor) creates the `worktree-agent-*` branch

Executor-reported `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` can be the agent's own post-commit tip rather than the true fork base — orchestrator must trust its own captured EXPECTED_BASE and verify via merge-base, not the agent's self-report
`close_phase_todos` only moves todos tagged `resolves_phase: N` in frontmatter; todos without that tag are stranded in pending even after the phase completes and requires manual reconciliation
web-e2e specs (writable-shares, shared-folder-desync, rotation-ux) require a live docker stack (API :3000, ipfs/redis/someguy/postgres/tee) and Playwright starts its own web server against it

In useSharedNavigationActions.ts, `seedActiveSharedFolder` calls must pass a real `publishedNode` (like navigateToShare, navigateToSubfolder, restoreToBreadcrumbIndex do) or it falls back to PLACEHOLDER_PUBLISHED_NODE and unsealNode throws a GCM decrypt error on retried writes

The 'resolveKinds-then-project' pattern across owned/shared nav (~9-10 sites) is not true duplication — each site has load-bearing differences (parallel vs sequential SDK calls, pre- vs post-await guards, > vs >= sequence checks, runWithFailureUx wrapping, writeKey-lifecycle side effects tied to specific SC/D-requirements) making unification high-risk with no real DRY payoff

code.finding: refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey's seedActiveSharedFolder call (originally lines 823-834) omitted publishedNode, unlike sibling call sites at lines 268, 410, 540 — fixed by passing getSdkClient().getSharedFolderState(currentShareId)?.publishedNode ?? PLACEHOLDER_PUBLISHED_NODE (commit d3c39c06e)
createAndPublishIpnsRecord now maps a 410 API status to {success:false, sequenceNumber:0n, tombstoned:true}, mirroring resolveIpnsRecord's existing 404-detection idiom

publishNodeFn (in buildWriteTransportSeams) checks pubResult.tombstoned===true and surfaces it before the generic failure throw; refreshSharedFolder's fresh branch now resolves and forwards publishedParent via resolvePublishedNode

handleDragStart's isFileRef(bareSealedChildRef) checks were unconditionally false since 68.2-11 kind-cache removal; replaced with isFileRefResolved(ref, resolvedByIpnsName) against the resolved listing map

workflow: Wave-based parallel worktree execution: capture base commit + build a wave manifest before dispatch, run intra-wave file-overlap checks pre-spawn (though undeclared incidental overlaps like comment-only touches can still slip through and must be caught at merge time)
After each wave: merge worktrees via cleanup-wave, run post-merge typecheck+test gate, update tracking (ROADMAP/STATE), then check advisory/blocking drift gates before starting next wave
After verifier reports gaps_found, independently re-confirm the specific claim against actual code before acting on it, rather than trusting the subagent verdict blindly
When delegating a risky behavior-neutral refactor to a subagent, give it a precise spec plus an explicit back-out clause (favor behavior-neutrality over completeness) and a mandatory local e2e gate

Independently re-verify a subagent's own verification claims (typecheck, e2e) rather than trusting its self-report, especially when the subagent's final message suggests it returned before confirming a backgrounded run's results
Convert a todo to a completed record with a resolution summary before moving it, rather than leaving self-contradictory 'still open' language in a file now filed as done

friction: Wave 1's 73-06 made an undeclared comment-only edit to useSharedWriteOps.ts, which 73-04 also modified — an intra-wave file overlap the pre-spawn declared-files check couldn't detect (needed git 3-way merge to resolve, which succeeded cleanly)
Post-merge gate commit-tracking helper reported 'commit_failed' as a false negative even though the commit actually landed, requiring manual git log verification each time

Full monorepo pnpm test/build defaults are unusable as a gate because they include live-API integration tests that fail without a running API — orchestrator had to manually scope gates to typecheck + specific affected package unit tests

73-08's WRITE-03 e2e case was never run live because it ran in a worktree parallel to 73-09, both defaulting to the same local ports (:3000, :5173), so starting a second dev-server risked disrupting the sibling agent — deferred to a documented non-blocking follow-up, and this exact gap is what the verifier later caught as a real bug
phase.complete's inline node-based JSON parsing attempt was malformed/syntax-broken twice, requiring fallback to writing raw output to a file and parsing cleanly
close_phase_todos moved 0 of 7 phase-73-related todos to completed because none were tagged with resolves_phase:73 in frontmatter, requiring manual investigation and reconciliation

A background/async agent task returned a premature 'still waiting' message before its final full report arrived in a later notification, requiring the orchestrator to independently verify e2e results in the interim rather than trust the incomplete status

API connection closed mid-response during the final todo-move/commit step, leaving the file edited but not yet git mv'd or committed, requiring the user to ask 'did that go through?' to catch the incomplete action
open_items: Live browser run of the rotation-ux WRITE-03 e2e case against a running local stack was never performed (deferred by 73-08 due to port contention with parallel 73-09) — remains a recommended CI/manual confirmation step even after the SC4 code fix and re-verification

Sub-item #2 of the consolidate-web-shared-navigation-dup todo (resolveKinds-then-project unification across ~9-10 owned+shared nav sites) was deliberately backed out as high-risk/low-value and left undone, with the analysis recorded in the now-completed todo as the resolution rather than pursued further
Milestone v2.0 (Metadata and Sharing Refactor) is fully complete (Phase 73 was its final phase) but not yet archived — /gsd-complete-milestone has not been run
Branch feat/shared-write-navigation-correctness-web has 47+ commits all local and unpushed; no PR opened yet (/gsd-ship 73 offered but not executed)
Final git mv of the todo file to completed/ and its commit were interrupted by a dropped API connection and had not been confirmed completed as of the end of the transcript
